Spinning blades can provide control to your craft.  Depending on how you place them, they will either use cyclic or collective pitch changes to apply torque.

This gives a range of control behaviour for your aircraft!

Cyclic mode is in effect when blades are aligned with the center of mass, and provides torque by changing the blade pitch as the blades rotate, so that the lift is different on either side of the rotor, creating torque.\r
Collective mode is in effect when blades are not aligned with the center of mass.  It provides torque by changing the blade pitch uniformly.

This special experiment collects data from planetary impacts. The amount of data depends on the size and speed of the object crashing into the surface and its distance from the seismometer - closer is better, up to a point.\r\n
Experiments like the Weather Station, Ion Detector and Mystery Goo Observation Unit collect data over time once deployed, powered and connected to a Control Station.\r\n
The amount of data an experiment generates per hour/impact is increased when deployed by a scientist, especially an experienced one

Once a Control Station has managed to generate some data it will be transmitted (by CommNet) back to Kerbin to generate Science.\r                                                  Use the Cargo System to move and place deployed science experiments.\r\n

The Deployed Science system is a set of experiments that can be deployed on the surface of a celestial body by a Kerbal to gather data over time. To generate data via  surface experiments, the player needs the following elements:\r\n
Enough deployed power parts to operate the other deployed units.
A Kerbal to set up the cluster of deployed parts.
One or more deployed experiment parts.
A Control Station.
